items.term: The common domain for two algebraic fractions

items.quote: you have previously learned the rational number which is in the form
items.text: The rational number in the form $\frac{a}{b}$ where $a, b \in Z$, $b \neq 0$. Given $p: R \to R$, $p(x) = x + 3$ and $f: R \to R$, $f(x) = x^2 - 4$.

items.quote: Find the domain of f and p .
items.text: Find the domain of f and p.

items.quote: can you find the domain of n when you know the
items.text: If $n(x) = \frac{p(x)}{f(x)}$ can you find the domain of n when you know the domain of each of p and f?

items.quote: From the previous, we deduce the following:
items.text: From the previous, we deduce the following:

items.quote: n is called an algebraic fractional function or an algebraic fraction
items.claim: n, where $n(x) = \frac{x+3}{x^2-4}$, is called an algebraic fractional function or an algebraic fraction.

items.quote: The domain in this case is R except for the values of x
items.claim: The domain is R except for the values of x which make the fraction undefined (the set of zeroes of the denominator).

items.quote: i.e : the domain of n(x) is R - {-2 , 2}
items.claim: The domain of n(x) is R - {-2, 2}.

items.quote: If p and f are two polynomail functions and z (f) is the set of zeroes
items.claim: If p and f are two polynomial functions and z(f) is the set of zeroes of f, then the function n: R - z(f) → R, n(x) = p(x)/f(x) is called a real algebraic fractional function, or briefly an algebraic fraction.

items.quote: the domain of algebraic fractional function = R - the set of zeroes of the denominator
items.claim: Note that: the domain of an algebraic fractional function = R - the set of zeroes of the denominator.

items.quote: The common domain of two or more algebraic fraction:
items.text: The common domain of two or more algebraic fraction:

items.quote: The set of real numbers where the fractions are identified together completely
items.claim: The common domain of two or more algebraic fractions is the set of real numbers where the fractions are identified together completely (at the same time).

items.quote: If n1 , n2 are two algebraic fractions where :
items.stem: If $n_1$, $n_2$ are two algebraic fractions where $n_1(x)=\frac{1}{x-1}$, $n_2(x)=\frac{3}{x^2-4}$ then calculate the common domain of $n_1$, $n_2$
solution: Let $m_1$ the domain of $n_1$, $m_2$ the domain of $n_2$.
$\therefore m_1=R-\{1\}$, $m_2=R-\{-2,2\}$ then the common domain of the two fractions $n_1,n_2=m_1\cap m_2$

items.quote: Remark : For any value of the variable x which belongs
items.text: Remark: For any value of the variable x which belongs to the common domain then, each of $n_1(x)$ and $n_2(x)$ are defined (existed).

items.quote: Generally :
then the common domain of the two fractions n1 and n2
items.claim: If $n_1$ and $n_2$ are two algebraic fractions, the domain of $n_1=R-X_1$ (where $X_1$ is the set of zeroes of the denominator of $n_1$) and the domain of $n_2=R-X_2$ (where $X_2$ is the set of zeroes of the denominator of $n_2$), then the common domain of the two fractions is $R-(X_1\cup X_2)$ = R - the set of zeroes of the two denominators of the two fractions.

items.quote: the common domain of a number of algebraic fractions
items.claim: The common domain of a number of algebraic fractions = R - the set of zeroes of the denominators of these fractions.

learning_objectives.label: Domain of algebraic fraction
learning_objectives.description: Determine the domain of an algebraic fractional function as R minus the set of zeroes of the denominator, and evaluate the function at given values.

learning_objectives.label: Common domain of fractions
learning_objectives.description: Calculate the common domain of two or more algebraic fractions as R minus the union of the zeroes of their denominators.
